errors.description: The model incorrectly identified the visible faces of each cube, which directly led to wrong inferences about the hidden faces. For example, in Cube 1, the model claimed Green, Red, and Yellow were visible — but according to the ground truth, the visible faces were Yellow (front), Blue (left), and Red (right), meaning Green was actually hidden. This misperception cascaded into a complete misassignment of hidden face colors across all cubes.

errors.description: Because the model started with a fundamentally incorrect assignment of visible vs. hidden faces, its subsequent counting and conclusion (that blue appears 5 times) was logically consistent within its own false premise — but factually wrong. analysis_result.analysis: The model failed due to a critical visual misidentification of the visible faces on each cube at frame 10. This led to an incorrect deduction of which faces were hidden, which in turn caused the model to assign wrong colors to the hidden faces. Although the model’s internal logic and counting were internally consistent, the entire reasoning chain was built on a false perceptual foundation.
